name: Identity Theft & Document Fraud
summary: Your ID number and personal documents are used to open accounts, take out credit and commit fraud in your name, often for years before you notice.

typicalLoss.note: The direct loss is often zero. The cost is a destroyed credit record and months of work proving you are not responsible.

targets: Anyone whose documents have been copied
Job seekers who sent document packs
People whose data appeared in a breach

howItWorks.detail: From fake job adverts, discarded copies, breached databases, corrupt insiders, or a stolen wallet. A certified ID copy and a proof of address is enough to start.

howItWorks.step: Credit is opened in your name
howItWorks.detail: Retail accounts, cellphone contracts, micro-loans and vehicle finance. Applications are spread across providers to avoid triggering a single alert.
Statements go elsewhere, so nothing arrives to warn you. This is why the fraud typically runs for a long time undetected.

howItWorks.step: You find out at the worst moment
howItWorks.detail: Usually when applying for a bond or a car, when a credit check reveals defaults and judgments you never incurred.

redFlags: Credit agreement or account statements arriving for products you never took out.
Being declined for credit when you expected approval.
Calls from debt collectors about accounts you do not recognise.
SMSes confirming a cellphone contract or delivery you did not order.
Post stops arriving, or a change-of-address confirmation you never requested.
illustrativeCase: A man who applied for warehouse work in 2024 and sent an ID copy, payslip and proof of address to a WhatsApp 'recruiter' is declined for a home loan in 2026. His credit report shows four retail accounts, two cellphone contracts and a personal loan, all opened in a province he has never lived in, all in default.
howToProtect: Register a free protective listing with the Southern African Fraud Prevention Service (SAFPS), which forces extra verification on any credit application in your name.
Check your credit report at least annually. You are entitled to a free report each year from each bureau.
Watermark every ID copy you hand over with the date and specific purpose.
Never send a selfie holding your ID unless you have independently verified who is asking and why.
Shred documents containing your ID number rather than binning them.
ifYouveBeenHit: Register a SAFPS protective listing immediately.
Dispute every fraudulent account in writing with the credit provider and the bureau. They must investigate.
Open a SAPS case, as providers will require the case number.
Get your credit report from all bureaus so you find every account, not just the one you noticed.

faqs.q: Am I liable for debt opened in my name?
faqs.a: Not if you can show it was fraudulent, but the burden of proving it falls largely on you. Documentation and a police case number are essential.

faqs.q: How long does it take to clear up?
faqs.a: Realistically months, and sometimes years across multiple providers. This is why prevention, particularly a SAFPS listing, is worth far more than remediation.
